messages:
sam: heads up — after today's runtime deploy I'm seeing a 3-4x tail latency spike on host-side. 95p for text-gen (HTTP/gRPC streaming) for requests with token_count >256 jumped from ~30ms to ~120ms. traces point to heavy time in parse/tokenize + a kernel selection fallback. anyone digging?

maya: saw the alerts too. getting repeated flame graphs from canary nodes — attached in #artifacts. looks concentrated in tokenize + request header parsing. :frowning: noticed more unicode-heavy payloads in the cohort.

arpit: quick note: we flipped kernel-selection heuristics in the last PR to prefer smaller kernels for long sequences (metrics: reduce GPU mem thrash) — could lead to more CPU-side work if we re-route. also soft-change in minibatching (aggressive mini-batch assemble) might amplify host parsing pressure.

ci-bot: deploy 2026-03-22T14:02 by arpit completed to canary cluster (3/10). automated perf checks flagged increased 95p for ingress-host parsing.

nina: I ran a microbench locally against the new tokenization path. results (median over 500 runs):
- payloads <256 tokens: tokenization ms: 3.9 -> 4.2 (noise)
- payloads 256-1024 tokens: tokenization ms: 4.2 -> 12.8 (regression)
Looks like utf8 normalization step got more expensive for longer inputs (maybe quadratic?).

maya: pprof (canary host) top lines:
```
25.3%  tokenization::utf8_normalize
18.7%  request::parse_headers
12.1%  runtime::kernel_selector::choose_fallback
9.6%   streaming::frame_assemble
6.8%   kvcache::lookup (miss path)
```
Consistent across several nodes.

arpit: kv cache telemetry also shows miss-rate jump: baseline ~2.1% -> now ~6.4% for the same qps. looks correlated with larger key lengths (we key by model+prefix hash which changed when we modified prefix normalization).

sam: ok — multiple contributing factors: tokenization (utf8), kernel fallback behavior, kv misses, and streaming frame sizing. we probably made several small changes that interacted badly. short-term mitigations?

devx: we can gate the new token normalization behind a feature flag and revert kernel-selection change in canary quickly. also I can patch streaming to use previous 2KB frame target instead of the new 512B when request token_count > 128.

perf-bot: metric snapshot: host-parse-ms (canary 3/10): p50 7.2ms -> 9.8ms, p95 31ms -> 118ms, kvcache_miss_rate: 2.1% -> 6.4%.

maya: proposed immediate action list:
1) revert utf8 normalization change in canary (maya)
2) add host-parse-ms histogram per-route + expose kernel-selection decision tag (devx)
3) revert kernel-selection heuristic change or add tighter gating (arpit)
4) restore streaming frame size for long requests (devx)
5) run targeted kvcache warmup / rebenchmark key hashing logic (nina)

arpit: +1. I'll open a rollback PR for kernel-selection and add a debug flag to log "chosen_kernel=..." for 1 minute on a sample of requests. I'll also run the kernel-selection microbench to see break-even thresholds.

nina: I'll instrument kvcache to emit key_length distribution and per-key ttl evictions. suspect the prefix-normalize change bumped key variety.

sam: action owners assigned: @maya revert tokenization change, @arpit revert/diagnose kernel selector, @nina kv telemetry, @devx streaming patch + metric surface. I'll coordinate rollback window — target 30m canary test then promote. adding a small postmortem ticket. :thumbsup:

maya: for the kernel selector probe we should capture seq_len, batch_size, chosen_kernel_id, cpu_parse_ms, gpu_exec_ms. that'll help model the tradeoffs.

devx: agreed. I'll add those tags to the request trace span.

sam: thanks all — monitoring now. will update once canary finishes.

(15:22) perf-bot: canary run after revert patch applied: 95p host-parse-ms down to ~34ms, kv miss back to ~2.3%. still watching streaming tail.

sam: great — keeping this open until we validate in prod.
